segments.text: Friends, in November 2021, lakhs of investors applied for what was then India's biggest IPO. Issue price: ₹2,150. On listing day, the share closed about 27% lower. The company was Paytm. And many of those investors had not checked a few simple things before clicking “Apply”.

Before you apply for the IPO, ask one question to yourself: where is my money going? Every IPO has two parts. The first part is Fresh Issue. Now in Fresh Issue, new shares are created and the money goes to the company, whether it is for expansion, for setting up new plants, or for the repayment of loans. The second part is Offer for Sale. Under OFS, existing shareholders sell their shares. Now the money goes to them, not to the company. As per SEBI's annual report, IPOs raised around ₹1.89 lakh crore in financial year 2025–26, and more than half of that was Offer for Sale. OFS is not always bad. But if promoters and early investors are selling a big chunk, ask yourself: if they are exiting at this price, why should I buy? Or why should I take entry into the stock? You will find this in the Objects of the Offer, which is a section of the Red Herring Prospectus. So the full checklist is available on the channel.
